transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-01
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Menon, Samir Patel (Redwood); Marta Alvarez, Ethan Kline, Ravi Nair, Nora Chen (HelixPay)
Shared artifacts: https://drive.google.com/helixpay-bridgecall-playbook (Jordan), https://redwood.com/docs/bridgecall-playbook (internal)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to align on postmortem follow-up from 2027-06-28 latency/partial-failure incident, finalize immediate mitigations, and plan a runbook rehearsal. Discussed warm standby, fallback routing, KV cache behavior, and how to keep customer-facing flows within SLO during backend degradation.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're going to run through a short triage playbook review and agree next steps after the 6/28 degradation event. Marta, do you want to kick off with a quick recap from your side?
00:18 Marta (HelixPay): Yeah, thanks. So, um, summary — payment flows saw increased tail latency, a subset of requests hit errors in our validation service, it seemed to cascade into the tokenization job. We saw a lot of retries, and that made things worse. We had a partial fallback to the on-prem vault but that added latency.
00:42 Ethan (HelixPay - Lead SRE): And to add, we had a KV cash invalidation event — sorry, KV cache — at 03:14 UTC, which caused a storm of cache misses. That spiked CPU on the Redwood Dedicated instance serving our models and that caused queueing.
01:05 Priya (Redwood SE): Quick clarification, when you say "Redwood Dedicated" — were you on the reserved node pool or did you have any burst to shared capacity? I wanna check routing.
01:18 Ethan: We were on reserved, but we had a fallback policy that briefly routed to the hosted tier; there was also a region failover attempt which made the requests cross AZs. Some headers were dropped.
01:35 Jordan: That's the exact set of things we want to codify in the bridgecall playbook: detection thresholds, who to page, what to check first, and when to flip the fallback policy.
01:48 Marta: The incident timeline in the PM was good but we need precise runbook steps for non-SRE folks — e.g., product or support can start a containment step.
02:05 Samir (Redwood CSM): We also want to avoid too many manual steps that only SRE can run; aim for 1-click mitigations wherever possible.
02:20 Ravi (Product): For product folks, what are the safe toggles? Is there a config to reduce model length or force shorter responses to cut token cost and latency?
02:35 Priya: Yes, you can set a hard max tokens header and also route to a lighter model variant. But there's a trade-off — shorter outputs can break downstream parsers. We'll document recommended parameter sets in the playbook.
03:00 Nora (Support): A bunch of customers reported timeouts; our support runbook had to escalate after 8 minutes. Can we make the public-facing timeout shorter to fail fast and show friendly messaging?
03:20 Jordan: Good point. Add to runbook: set a visible UX timeout at 3s client side and have server-level SLO 5s. We'll include templates for user messaging.
03:40 Speaker 1: (inaudible) -- packet capture and logs are in the ticket but need to be correlated to the traces.
04:05 Priya: On the technical side, two high-value mitigations we discussed: 1) add a KV cache warm-up and prefix-caching to reduce cold miss storms, 2) add auto-throttling on retry loops upstream so retries don't amplify the problem.
04:28 Ethan: For the KV cache warm-up, we have a scheduled job but it didn't cover the full keyspace; we need a coverage report. We'll attach that.
04:45 Jordan: We'll include a 'coverage check' step in the playbook and a quick command snippet to run to verify.
05:10 Marta: Can Redwood help with a short-run bench to show how changed retry backoff and cache warm-up affect latency? A kind of before/after with our traffic patterns.
05:28 Priya: Yes, we can run a tailored micro-benchmark on Dedicated to simulate your distribution and share results. We'll need sample traces and a representative traffic histogram.
05:45 Ethan: We'll provide a day-of traffic histogram and top 10 request IDs that hit errors.
06:00 Jordan: Great. Now on escalation — who is the primary bridge lead and who is the SME? For Redwood, Jordan will be bridge lead, Priya as SE SME, Samir as customer liaison. For HelixPay, Marta will be primary, Ethan backup.
06:22 Marta: Confirmed. Also we want an runbook roles doc so Support can follow a checklist.
06:40 Priya: We'll produce a one-page roles and responsibilities sheet.
07:05 Jordan: Let's walk the playbook steps quickly — Detection -> Validate -> Contain -> Mitigate -> Recover -> Postmortem. For detection, we recommend a 3x baseline increase in p95 or any increase in 5xx rate above 0.5% triggers the bridge.
07:40 Ethan: Our alarms are currently at 10x baseline and too slow. We'll lower thresholds and add a synthetic that hits a hot path.
08:00 Ravi: About fallback routing — what about the cost and consistency tradeoffs? If we route to hosted, we lose data isolation guarantees for that traffic, right?
08:12 Jordan: Correct — routing to hosted tier is a temporary emergency measure. The playbook will include an approval step for PII-handling traffic and a checklist to redact or limit payloads.
08:32 Priya: Also, for private deployments, the KMS/HSM keys can't be used in hosted fallback, so we suggest a policy to only route non-sensitive requests unless customer has explicit waiver.
08:50 Marta: We will not allow payment-tokenizing requests to be routed to hosted. That's non-negotiable.
09:05 Jordan: We'll codify that in the 'safe to fallback' table in the doc.
09:20 Samir: One other note, some of the internal product names get mistranscribed in support notes. The incident log said "Redwood Dedicate" in places; we should standardize naming so automation picks up the right runbook.
09:40 Priya: ha, yes "Redwood Dedicate" is a classic. We'll add canonical names.
10:00 Ethan: On mitigations, adding circuit breakers upstream is low-cost and high-impact. We implemented a brief rate limit on retries during last incident which helped but it was manual.
10:20 Priya: We'll add a template for an automatic circuit-breaker rule that flips after X errors in Y seconds and suggests backoff windows.
10:40 Marta: Regarding observability, our traces had gaps around the cache layer. Are there any recommended tracing hooks or sampling adjustments?
10:55 Priya: Yes, increase sampling for error traces to 100% for the hot path during incidents and add a KV cache span. We'll send an instrumentation snippet for your tracer.
11:20 Nora: Support also asked for a user-friendly incident status template we can paste into Zendesk. Can Redwood provide a templated status message?
11:35 Jordan: We'll include that and a short FAQ for common customer questions during a bridge.
11:50 Ravi: Security question: do any of these mitigations change compliance posture (SOC 2, data residency)? We need that on the checklist.
12:05 Samir: Anything that routes outside VPC or to hosted will require a documented approval and a brief audit note; we'll add a step to capture that and notify security.
12:25 Marta: Good. On the follow-ups: we want the runbook rehearsal where we simulate a KV cache miss storm and practice containment. Can Redwood lead that?
12:40 Priya: Yes, we can run a rehearsal. We propose a 60-min session: 15-min scenario briefing, 30-min run, 15-min retro.
12:58 Jordan: We'll draft the scenario and share it.
13:10 Ethan: One last technical ask — can Redwood check the Hot Path throttle config on your side? I saw a parameter that might allow more aggressive preemption of long-running requests.
13:26 Priya: We'll check and recommend a tuned config. Also we'll share a fallback policy for long-run requests: either cancel or return partial results with a retry token.
13:45 Marta: Trade-offs are tricky but returning partial results with a token for rehydration sounds acceptable. We'll discuss UX implications.
14:05 Speaker 2 (partial): (overlap) -- are we going to store those tokens?
14:20 Jordan: Short-lived tokens stored in your K/V store, yes. We'll add encryption guidance.
14:35 Ethan: For the packet captures and logs, where should we upload? We put in the support ticket but I'd rather have a shared secure folder.
14:50 Jordan: Use the support ticket for initial upload and we'll move to a secure Redwood share; we'll provide upload instructions in the action item.
15:10 Priya: Ok, to recap action items: we'll share playbook, runbench, KV diagnostic, packet traces; runbook rehearsal scheduled. Any blockers?
15:28 Marta: None. Just please include the 'no-hosted-for-tokenize' rule.
15:40 Jordan: Noted.
15:50 Samir: I'll follow up with calendar invites and make sure we have the right stakeholders.
16:05 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll send the playbook draft and set the rehearsal invite.
16:20 Meeting ends.
